text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Joint Moslem-Croat police in the Neretva Canton must be established first if Bosnia's collective presidency chairman Alija Izetbegovic is to meet Croatian President Franjo Tudjman, in Croatia soon, says Bosnian ambassador to Croatia, Kasim Trnka.
- First train from Serb held town of Doboj arrives in Moslem-Croat town of Tuzla after a five-year pause caused by the Bosnian war.
- In 1996 Croatian exports to Bosnia totalled $470 million while imports from Bosnia amounted only to $70 million, government officials say.

- Munib Jusufovic, Moslem mayor of disputed town of Brcko in exile tells international supervisor in town Robert Farrand that he is not going to be coming to Farrand's office in Brcko in future because of the poor security and a recent stoning of Moslem refugees buses.

- Bosnia's foreign minister Croat Jadranko Prlic says a protest letter that his Moslem deputy sent to Croatia over recent diplomatic incidents in Mostar and Bihac was his deputy's personal opinion. --Sarajevo newsroom, 387-71-663-864.
